story: On a sunny October Sunday afternoon at 1:17 on Magnolia Loop in Sumter Oaks, Rosa catches Gary and Donna and sets dinner for six o'clock at her place, with Hal invited too. Gary apologizes for mixing up the evening, promising he and Donna will finish their pickleball rally and come over hungry, while Donna cheerfully hurries them toward court one. Hal, sounding gruff but sheepish, admits the day got away from him and asks Rosa to keep the roast warm, and Rosa, relieved and hopeful, sends everyone off to play well.

gary.thought_process: Rosa just said she waited with a cooling pork roast for me, Hal, and Donna, and I told her at tick 92 to save us a table tonight. Looks like she got the day wrong, or I did. Donna's here too, and we haven't played yet. I shouldn't repeat myself, so I'll clear up the mix-up with Rosa: pickleball with Donna first, then we'll come eat, and the roast won't go to waste. Also, I filed the cart form already, so Hal's notice is something to sort out later.

parameters.content: Rosa, that's on me, I thought you meant tonight. Donna and I will finish our rally and come straight over, and I'll eat enough for Hal too.

donna.thought_process: We just rolled up to Magnolia Loop in the cart, and Gary headed here too. Last I said, I'd drive us to court one by noon and treat him to Rosa's after, and it's already past 1:15, so I'm running behind. Gary, Hal, and Rosa are all in view, and Rosa is right here, so I can do a little social work while I get Gary moving. I already invited him and he agreed, so I shouldn't re-ask. I'll nudge him to hop in so we actually get to the rec center, and mention Rosa's so she hears we're headed that way afterward.

parameters.content: Okay, Gary, we're officially behind schedule, so paddle in the cart and let's roll to court one. Rosa's gets us afterward, and I want your footwork warm before the ladder match.

hal.thought_process: Rosa is right here and just told me she's been sitting with a cooling pork roast for three people. I posted my notice last tick, so the paperwork's handled. A man who leaves a woman waiting over a roast is no sergeant of mine. I never confirmed dinner, and she's owed a straight answer. Besides, the grumbling can wait until after the meal. Order and respect cut both ways.

parameters.content: Day got away from me, Rosa. That's on me, not you. Keep that roast warm and I'll be along shortly.

rosa.thought_process: It's 1:17 PM and the dinner is tonight. Earlier I assumed the date was today and sat with a cooling pork roast, but Gary just told me to save a table for tonight, so they all think it's tonight. I didn't misread the date, I just got the time wrong. Hal, Gary, and Donna are all standing right here on Magnolia Loop, which is the best chance to lock in the plan. I already asked Hal at tick 92 and shouldn't repeat that. Gary's answer was a yes. Donna just arrived and I haven't spoken to her yet. I'll invite her directly and give a clear time so all three show up together.

parameters.content: Donna, good, I've got you and Gary both in one spot. Dinner at my place tonight at six, Hal's coming too. Go win your pickleball, then come hungry.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
